summary.headline: NRB Bearings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13% YoY to INR372 crores, EBITDA margin 19.5%, and FY26 PAT up 77% to INR146 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR372 crores, with EBITDA up 17% to INR74 crores (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR42 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 11% to INR1,335 crores, EBITDA rose 19% to INR267 crores, and margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3%. Management attributed margin gains to solar power, automation, yield improvement and renegotiated vendor costs, and flagged a quarter-end forex anomaly that pulled down Q4 gross margin. Management leaned on an FY-level lens, declined to disclose standalone export, aftermarket, and segment splits, and guided to brownfield capacity commissioning from June-July 2026.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Management says NRB is in transmission, driveline, chassis and steering, with limited engine exposure beyond two- and three-wheelers and little wheel-end content. Replacement market grew about 4%, and the company said it shifted focus toward OEMs in Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial business is about 14-15% of revenue per management, including tractors and farm equipment. Target is 20-25% of revenue over time; named focus areas are construction equipment, off-highway, gearboxes, switchgear, power generation and electric grid.

segments.name: Aerospace (Mahant Toolroom, acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mahant Toolroom order book is close to INR50 crores, up from INR25 crores at announcement, with all orders from HAL across divisions. Management expects full operational control between mid-April and May 2026 and a business plan in about six months.

guidance_outlook: International business expected to grow 10-14% in FY27 per current business plan, with management saying maybe up to 15%.

FY27 capex guided at about INR120 crores (including land), against a total announced INR200 crore capex over 18 months plus up to INR40 crores for land; split is 90% machines and 10% infrastructure and building.
Brownfield capacity enhancements to commission from June-July 2026 through FY27 and up to Q1 2028, with partial benefits from the current quarter.
Management aims to sustain EBITDA margins of 18-21% over time; industrial products expected to be as profitable as the core, with individual products ranging from 14% to 30%.
Five-year aspirational revenue target of about INR2,500 crores, which management said is increasingly becoming a concrete goal.
Mahant Toolroom business plan to be shared in about six months; AS9100-linked aerospace certification expected in about six months.
capex_capacity: Reported capacity utilisation about 85%; management says effective utilisation at several plants is much closer to full after adjusting for demand variation, maintenance, shifts and changeovers.
Bottlenecks identified at specific plants; machinery orders placed and first machines arrived, with major enhancement commissioning from June-July 2026.
Capex split: about 90% machines and 10% infrastructure/building/plant; maintenance, quality, new product and small balancing capex is part of normal capex at about 10% of turnover.
Joint venture declaration allows up to 20% of JV capacity to be used for automotive; about 20-25% of current automotive capacity is being used for industrial products.
Mahant Toolroom acquisition gives people, design and certification capability; the company had INR100 crores of aerospace RFQs but lacked an AS9100 plan.
demand_pricing: Management says growth came from volume, market share gains, capacity utilisation, product mix and efficiency, not one-offs.
Export demand was affected by geopolitics and logistics; India faced gas shortages, and customers changed product mix during Q4, which reduced the quarter's original plan.
Management says it prices to maintain margin profile; EV-specific bearings priced to keep existing margins and bearing content per vehicle is largely value neutral.
Company does not give export, aftermarket or standalone splits; it says the replacement market grew about 4% and that it deprioritised replacement given discount structures.
New wins include Siemens (details withheld under confidentiality), and aerospace platforms for HAL and NAL.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4% international growth standalone exports, and what are export and aftermarket growth for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reports consolidated international business (all overseas-supplied customers, including subsidiaries) at about 4% growth and declined to give standalone export or aftermarket figures; replacement market grew about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex, and what is the split between standalone and subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for FY27 is closer to INR120 crores, including land; management declined to split standalone versus subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin dip, the first sub-60% quarter in a long time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it primarily to forex, combining product mix with high-import-content products and quarter-end rupee conversion of COGS; it said this is an accounting anomaly that should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Mahant's INR50 crore order book will convert in FY27, and is HAL 100% of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 revenue and said the order book pace depends on rollout rates; HAL is the sole customer but across multiple divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Will industrial be margin accretive, and when will industrial reach 20% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial products are expected to match the company's 18-20% EBITDA requirement, averaging out over five years; industrial is 14-15% of revenue today and the aim is 20-25%, with no firm timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR120 crore capex and maintenance capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the INR200 crore 18-month plan plus INR40 crore land; maintenance capex sits within normal capex at about 10% of turnover.

risks_watch: Q4 gross margin dipped below 60% on forex and product mix; management says this should normalise, so watch the Q1 FY27 gross margin.
Capacity commissioning from June-July 2026 is central to volume growth; monitor timing and the realised utilisation levels.
International growth guidance of 10-14% (up to 15%) follows 4% in FY26; watch whether export demand recovers.
Mahant Toolroom order book conversion, AS9100 certification timing (about six months), and the business plan promised in about six months.
Management withheld several data points (standalone exports, aftermarket, segment mix, capex split), limiting analyst verification.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on structural margin gains and long-term strategy, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to give segment, export, aftermarket, and capex-split figures. It acknowledged the Q4 forex-driven margin dip and softer demand from the Middle East and gas shortages without giving quantified impact.
key_quotes: We are satisfied with the quality of growth.
At no point, at no point did we fail to meet key customer commitments. That for us is non -negotiable.
We compete on engineering capability, we compete on flexibility, and we compete by driving this with an immensely disciplined process-oriented approach.
So, as I mentioned in a five-year timeframe we would be around 2,500 crores.

adds.what: Brownfield capacity enhancements at bottleneck plants (part of INR200 crore capex over 18 months)

growth.why: Management guides international business growth of 10-14% in FY27 per current business plan and a INR2,500 crore five-year aspiration, backed partly by machine orders already arrived, brownfield commissioning from June-July 2026 and Mahant Toolroom order book near INR50 crore, but no consolidated FY27 revenue guidance was given and the aspiration is unquantified by timeline detail.
